I have been farming these 18 mu in Quzhou for 45 years, since I was a boy following my father around the fields. Cotton is what I know best — it is my main cropping system and my main source of cash. The rest of my land I keep in the wheat–maize rotation for household grain and feed. With six mouths to feed and some of my family working off-farm, I cannot afford to gamble on strange new methods. I stick to what this land and I have learned together.

This spring, my wheat is already in the ground from last October. I rotary-tilled before sowing and put down basal compound fertilizer then. Now I will topdress with urea at green-up and irrigate three times from my well — at green-up, jointing, and heading. I use improved wheat varieties from the county seed station, about 30 jin of seed per mu. I will spray twice for aphids and rust. I expect about 1000 jin per mu.

My cotton will go on 8 mu. I will rotary till in late April, then plant improved cotton seed — guoxinmian or lumianyan, about 2.5 jin per mu. I spread 100 jin of compound fertilizer as a base before sowing, and I will topdress with urea once when flowering starts. Cotton is thirsty and pest-prone here; I will irrigate twice and spray insecticide about 12 times through the season. If the weather cooperates, I expect around 550 jin of seed cotton per mu.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant summer maize on those same 5 mu. I use hybrid seed — denghai or woyu, about one package per mu. I plant directly into the wheat stubble with no tillage; that saves diesel and time when the summer heat is coming. I put down compound fertilizer at planting. I will irrigate twice if the summer rains are thin, and spray twice for corn borer. I expect about 950 jin per mu.
